risks.name: Prompt Injection
risks.why: LLM/generative system exposed to untrusted or retrieved input
risks.summary: Crafted inputs (direct or indirect, e.g. via retrieved content) alter the model's behaviour, bypassing instructions or controls.
risks.severity_rationale: retrieval runs over a user-modifiable knowledge base, enabling indirect injection (arch_rag_modifiable=yes).
risks.mitigation: Constrain and validate inputs, separate system/user content, least-privilege tool access, output filtering, and human approval for high-impact actions.

risks.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
risks.why: processes personal/special-category data that could be disclosed
risks.summary: The model reveals confidential data (training data, PII, secrets) through its outputs or via inference attacks.
risks.severity_rationale: retrieval runs over a user-modifiable knowledge base, enabling indirect injection (arch_rag_modifiable=yes).
risks.mitigation: Data minimisation, scrubbing/PII redaction, output filtering, access controls, and limiting memorisation.

risks.name: Data and Model Poisoning
risks.why: ingests untrusted external/user data that could poison the model
risks.summary: Manipulated training/fine-tuning/embedding data introduces backdoors, bias or degraded integrity.
risks.severity_rationale: a user-modifiable RAG corpus can be poisoned (arch_rag_modifiable=yes).
risks.mitigation: Vet data sources, integrity checks, anomaly detection on training data, and provenance tracking.

risks.name: System Prompt Leakage
risks.why: uses a system prompt that may leak
risks.summary: Disclosure of system prompts exposes secrets, logic or controls that were wrongly relied upon for security.
risks.severity_rationale: retrieval runs over a user-modifiable knowledge base, enabling indirect injection (arch_rag_modifiable=yes).
risks.mitigation: Never put secrets/authz logic in the system prompt; enforce controls server-side and assume the prompt is public.

risks.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
risks.why: likely uses embeddings/RAG over sensitive or external content
risks.summary: Weaknesses in RAG vector stores/embeddings enable data leakage, poisoning of retrieved context, or access bypass.
risks.severity_rationale: retrieval runs over a user-modifiable knowledge base, enabling indirect injection (arch_rag_modifiable=yes).
risks.mitigation: Access-control and tenant-isolate the vector store, validate ingested documents, and audit retrieval.

risks.name: Supply Chain
risks.why: relies on third-party/foundation models or external components
risks.summary: Vulnerabilities in third-party models, datasets, plugins or dependencies compromise integrity or security.
risks.severity_rationale: baseline risk; not strongly amplified by the stated architecture.
risks.mitigation: Vet and pin model/dataset/dependency provenance, verify signatures, maintain an SBOM/AIBOM, scan dependencies.

risks.name: Misinformation
risks.why: generative output may be inaccurate (hallucination) yet relied upon
risks.summary: Hallucinated or biased output is relied upon as fact, causing harm or unsafe decisions.
risks.severity_rationale: baseline risk; not strongly amplified by the stated architecture.
risks.atlas_note: Partly a safety/trust issue outside ATLAS's attack scope.
risks.mitigation: Grounding/RAG with citations, uncertainty signalling, human review, and clear AI-output labelling.

risks.name: Unbounded Consumption
risks.why: exposed/large-scale: vulnerable to resource exhaustion or extraction
risks.summary: Uncontrolled resource use (inference flooding, model extraction, cost harvesting) causes denial of service or cost.
risks.severity_rationale: rate limits / quotas are in place (arch_rate_limits=yes).
risks.mitigation: Rate limiting and quotas, input/size limits, monitoring and alerting on anomalous usage.

risks.name: Improper Output Handling
risks.why: output reaches downstream systems (or tools/actions) without review
risks.summary: Unvalidated model output is passed to downstream systems (code, SQL, shell, browsers), enabling injection/XSS/RCE.
risks.severity_rationale: read-only and no unreviewed downstream actions → integrity risk re-rated to Low.
risks.atlas_note: No dedicated ATLAS technique; modelled as an injection-driven downstream chain.
risks.mitigation: Treat model output as untrusted: encode/escape, validate against schemas, and sandbox downstream execution.

risks.name: Excessive Agency
risks.why: can autonomously take actions or call tools
risks.summary: Excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy lets the system take damaging actions on ambiguous or manipulated input.
risks.severity_rationale: read-only and no unreviewed downstream actions → integrity risk re-rated to Low.
risks.atlas_note: No single ATLAS technique; modelled as a chain (injection vector -> downstream action/impact).
risks.mitigation: Least-privilege tools/permissions, human-in-the-loop for consequential actions, and bounded scopes.

answers._comment: Synthetic example - a health insurer's GenAI customer-service assistant on a hosted foundation model (deployer), RAG over policy conditions, with tools that look up the caller's own claim status. Limited risk (Art. 50 disclosure) — but health data in prompts, an external model provider (DORA), agentic tool calls and a 'not yet approved' governance status make it the case that looks easy and is not.
answers.sys_name: Meridian Health member service assistant (read-only pilot)
answers.sys_owner: Example Health Insurer N.V. — Customer Contact
answers.sys_description: A chat assistant on a hosted large language model that answers insured persons' questions about coverage and claims, retrieves the policy conditions and, after login, looks up the caller's own claim status through an internal API.
answers.intended_purpose: First-line answers to coverage and claim-status questions; hand-off to a human agent for anything else. No decisions on coverage or payment.
answers.data_sources: Policy conditions (public), help-centre articles, claim-status API (per caller), chat transcripts.
answers.human_oversight: Agents monitor a live queue and can take over any conversation; a weekly sample of transcripts is scored for correctness; a wrong-answer report button is shown under every reply.
answers.dg_data_owner: Head of Customer Contact (data domain: customer interaction)
answers.dg_lineage: Policy conditions + help-centre CMS -> chunk + embed (nightly) -> vector store -> ZorgChat (hosted model, EU region) -> answer -> chat widget; claim-status tool: caller identity -> claims API (read-only) -> answer
answers.dg_q_evidence: Knowledge-base freshness: nightly sync, max age 24 h (measured). Answer correctness sample: 94% (weekly review, 2026-08).

gov_exceptions.exception: Pilot with 5% of web-chat traffic before the approval decision
gov_exceptions.decision: Allowed with human take-over on every escalation and daily transcript review
